{"id":"PKIX-ew5w","title":"Five beads held by abandoned bd-spin agent claims cannot be closed without --force","description":"Found while reconciling the duplicated-bead pairs (PKIX-29bc follow-on work, 2026-11-25).

Five beads carry an assignee of the form 'bd-spin/bd-spin-<timestamp>-<pid>', an agent identity from May 2026 that was never released:

  PKIX-jbvb      blocked   bd-spin-20260513T202312Z-3017126
  PKIX-jbvb.9.1  open      bd-spin-20260514T024333Z-3287470
  PKIX-hbzo      open      bd-spin-20260511T212242Z-1478141
  PKIX-ng0x      blocked   bd-spin-20260511T043138Z-4160815
  PKIX-xj81      blocked   bd-spin-20260511T043138Z-4160815

The practical effect is a trap rather than a cosmetic wart: bd refuses both 'bd unclaim' and 'bd close' on a bead held by a different actor, so anyone finishing this work hits 'cannot close: assignee is bd-spin/..., actor is <you>; reclaim or use --force to override' and has to know about --force. PKIX-gphz.1 was in the same state and blocked closing a duplicate until force-unclaimed.

Note the two sharing 4160815: one crashed agent took both PKIX-ng0x and PKIX-xj81 and never came back.

Fix is mechanical -- 'bd unclaim <id> --force' on each -- but it is someone's deliberate call rather than a sweep to run blind, because releasing a claim is a statement that nobody is working the item. Six months of silence from an agent process ID is good evidence of that, and the claims should probably just go.

Worth checking at the same time whether anything in the workflow re-creates these: if an agent run claims beads and exits without unclaiming, the board accumulates this indefinitely. A crash-safe claim (lease with expiry) would be the real fix; 'bd doctor' may already have an opinion.","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"chore","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-25T17:51:58.090478884Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-25T17:51:58.090478884Z"}

new_value:
All five released, and the root cause turned out to be more specific than the bead guessed.

NOT done with 'bd unclaim --force', which this bead proposed. That resets status to 'open', and 'blocked' is a STORED status here, not derived: three of the five (PKIX-jbvb, PKIX-ng0x, PKIX-xj81) are blocked by real 'blocks' dependencies on open children, and unclaiming would have cleared the assignee AND flipped them to open, pushing them into 'bd ready' as falsely workable. That is worse than leaving them stuck.

Used 'bd update <id> --assignee ""' instead, which clears the assignee without touching status and -- usefully -- is not subject to the actor-mismatch refusal that blocks unclaim and close. Verified after: all five unassigned, PKIX-hbzo and PKIX-jbvb.9.1 still open, the other three still blocked and still reported by 'bd list --status=blocked', and nothing leaked into ready (8 blocked, 100 ready).

ROOT CAUSE. bd already has the lease machinery this bead speculated about: 'bd heartbeat' refreshes a lease, 'bd reclaim' is the reaper for dead workers. But reclaim only touches IN_PROGRESS issues whose lease expired -- these five were open or blocked while still carrying an assignee, so they sat outside what the reaper can see. A claim that survives a status change back to open/blocked is invisible to recovery. That is the gap worth fixing upstream, not the absence of a reaper.

Secondary finding: 'bd doctor' reports 14/14 checks passed with five beads in this state. A stale-assignee check on non-in_progress issues would have surfaced it; worth suggesting upstream.

Scope note: 131 bd-spin assignees remain, all on CLOSED beads. Those are left alone deliberately -- on a closed issue the assignee is the record of who did the work, not a claim blocking anyone.
